c001.heard: Every morning, a committee of egg farmers puts out a number. On twenty ninth October twenty twenty six, at Namakkal in Tamil Nadu, it was five rupees seventy paise for an egg.

c002.heard: That number began with another morning, fifty seven years earlier, and six hens that a postmaster carried to the vet.

c003.heard: How did six hens become a price? It took four tries. Each one fixed a problem, and made the next.

c005.heard: Namakkal sits in the middle of Tamil Nadu. In the late nineteen sixties it was part of Salem district. A university case study calls it a place with low levels of agricultural activity.

c006.heard: In nineteen sixty nine, a village postmaster named V. Vellappan brought six red desi hens to the government veterinary hospital in Namakkal.

c007.heard: Desi hens are hardy. But they lay few eggs.

c008.heard: So the vet, Doctor N. Nandagopal, suggested hybrid layers instead. More eggs. More manure for the fields. More income.

c010.heard: In nineteen seventy the vet drove Vellappan and three other farmers to a poultry firm in Coimbatore. They bought four hundred chicks, at three or four rupees each.

c011.heard: Each farmer raised one hundred chicks in a thatched shed. And every morning, the vet came to check them, free of cost.

c012.heard: The hens grew. They laid. And the town turned up its nose.

c013.heard: Consumers and restaurant owners, the study says, wanted only desi eggs.

c014.heard: Four farmers, each with a shed full of eggs nobody local wanted, and eggs do not wait. Sell alone, and take whatever a buyer offers. Or sell together.

c015.heard: The vet's answer, form a farm club. Collect everyone's eggs, and sell them together, further away.

c016.heard: The club sent eggs to Chennai by train and sold them for twenty two paise each.

c018.heard: Farmers from nearby villages came to see. Sheds went up everywhere. The study counts about three lakh birds in the mid seventies, twelve lakh a few years later, and thirty lakh by nineteen eighty two.

c019.heard: But more hens means more eggs, every single day. When too many arrive at once, the price falls, and every farmer stands alone against the buyer.

c020.heard: Around 1981, the Egg Committee's own history says, feed had become 250% dearer in five years, and eggs still sold for about 35 paise. More than 40% of poultry farmers had stopped.

c021.heard: So, the club could sell eggs. It could not stop the price from falling.

c023.heard: In Namakkal, P. K. Venkatachalam, one of the early farmers, recalled taking a van of eggs to Chennai at an agreed nineteen paise. The trader offered fifteen. They settled at seventeen.

c024.heard: Within a week, Venkatachalam said, the farmers met and formed a Namakkal committee to set the price. Farmers from Hyderabad, Chittoor and Pune joined, and it became national.

c025.heard: and the national committee's own history tells it through the breeder Doctor B. V. Rao, who travelled the country and held more than three hundred meetings

c026.heard: with one slogan, my egg, my price, my life.

c027.heard: On the fourteenth of May nineteen eighty two, the National Egg Coordination Committee began declaring the price of eggs. Not a government body, an association of poultry farmers.

c028.heard: By nineteen eighty five, the study counts seventy five lakh birds around Namakkal. That year the town got its own veterinary college.

c030.heard: A price set by producers has a problem of its own. Is it fair for sellers to agree on a price together? In twenty seventeen, two complaints reached the Competition Commission of India.

c031.heard: In January twenty twenty two the Commission found that the committee's price is the de facto price in the market, because no other body in India declares one. Fifty years earlier, nobody wanted their eggs. Now nobody else was naming a price.

c032.heard: It held that trying to enforce the price, with penalties or the threat of them, broke the competition law. It ordered an end to such threats, and told the committee to call its prices only suggestive. It imposed no fine. An appeal asking for penalties was dismissed by the tribunal, and a further appeal is pending in the Supreme Court.

c034.heard: Today, Tamil Nadu's own count puts Namakkal at about four crore eggs a day, two of every three eggs in the state.

c035.heard: And the eggs went abroad. In twenty twenty five, India's egg exports were the highest on record, nearly eighteen crore eggs a month, most of them to the Gulf.

c036.heard: Eggs still do not wait. In March 2026, with Gulf shipping in crisis, India's egg exports fell by 7 tenths.

c037.heard: And Namakkal's rate fell to three rupees eighty five.

c038.heard: In July it reached six eighty, the highest on NECC's daily sheets since twenty twenty two. By late August, five twenty.

c039.heard: In thirteen of the last sixteen years, the cheapest month was March or April.

c040.heard: The club's first eggs sold for twenty two paise. This week's suggestion is five rupees seventy.

c041.heard: In nineteen seventy, a vet came every morning to check the hens. Today, every morning, the farmers' own committee puts out a number. Only a suggestion. But it is the one the trade reads first.
